key_insight: A multi-aspect, multi-agent framework (MAMA-Memeia) plus the RESTOREx resource enables reliable identification of depressive symptoms in memes by jointly modeling visual cues, text, and symptom-specific signals rather than treating memes as simple sentiment units.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of detecting clinically-relevant depressive symptoms in multimodal memes on social media, where meaning arises from interactions between image and text and standard sentiment models fail to capture symptom-level signals.
method: Multi-aspect modeling: extract and integrate complementary signals from image content, overlaid text, and contextual/meta features to capture symptom expressions.
Multi-agent collaboration: specialized agents (e.g., visual agent, textual/LLM agent, symptom classifier) cooperate to produce symptom-level labels and resolve cross-modal ambiguities.
Resource + annotation pipeline: introduce RESTOREx, a curated dataset and annotation strategy for depressive symptoms in memes to train and evaluate the system.
impact: Provides a scalable multimodal approach and a dedicated dataset that enable more precise, symptom-level mental-health detection from memes—useful for researchers building ethically-aware monitoring tools, dataset benchmarks, and intervention pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing multi-agent pipeline (visual agent, textual/LLM agent, fusion module, symptom classifier).
Annotated meme examples with overlays mapping image/text cues to specific depressive symptoms.
Dataset summary chart (class distribution across symptoms, sample counts) to illustrate RESTOREx coverage.
Performance snapshot (precision/recall or bar chart) comparing multi-agent approach vs. baseline multimodal models.
paper_title: MAMA-Memeia! Multi-Aspect Multi-Agent Collaboration for Depressive Symptoms Identification in Memes
paper_authors: Siddhant Agarwal, Adya Dhuler, Polly Ruhnke, Melvin Speisman, Md Shad Akhtar
